variants.structure: contradiction (camera vs eyes) → photo proof → not giant → farther → leading explanation → still debated → fingernail test → paper tube + integrated save CTA (8 beats)

beats.text: Your camera says the Moon never grew.
beats.visual_intent: frame 0: giant moon over rooftops, a camera pointing at it

beats.text: Photos with the same settings show it the same width, low or high.
beats.visual_intent: two photos side by side, equal-width rulers

beats.text: Down low, it's actually about 1.5 percent farther away.
beats.visual_intent: night: eye, distance line to the low moon

beats.text: A leading explanation: your brain judges the horizon Moon farther away, so it sees it bigger.
Scientists still argue about the exact cause.
Test it: at arm's length, a fingernail covers about the same amount of Moon, low or high.
beats.visual_intent: night: a fingernail beside the low moon and the high moon, same size

beats.text: Or look through a rolled-up paper tube, and the giant Moon shrinks. Save this for the next big Moon.
beats.visual_intent: night: view through a paper tube, a small moon; then a big SAVE label

title_options: Your camera says the Moon never grew
The giant horizon Moon isn't bigger
publish.description: Same-setting photos show the horizon Moon the same width as the high Moon, and it is about 1.5 percent farther away. A leading explanation: your brain.

cta.decision_reason: the video ends on two tests viewers can only do on a moonrise night; saving it is the useful next step
cta.spoken: Save this for the next big Moon.
